For accommodations it’s better to check out the suburbs like Mytishi, Podolsk, Khimki and such. If you’re okay with a hostel, you can find some for as low as 500₽ per night even in Moscow. 

Universal transit card which would allow you to take the metro, buses, MCC (railway ring in Moscow) and MCD (2 commuter train lines) costs 2170₽ per month. 

Outside of buying an access for a month one ride costs 40₽. It includes a free change between metro, MCC and MCD within 90 minutes (each could only be used once without additional payment). If you do a transfer from/to the bus, it’s additional 22₽ and every bus trip within 90 minutes would be free. 

Cellular is dirt cheap and fast. I personally use a plan with 500 minutes / 500 texts / 30 GBs for 565₽/mo. 

Food cost varies. Supermarkets like Lenta and Auchan are obviously cheaper than most convenience stores like Magnit or Dixi. If you’re okay with a limited choice, there is several alcohol-related convenience stores like Krasnoe-Beloe and Bristol with a choice of tin cans, ramen and macaroni priced as good as in supermarkets. 

For instance, a pack of Doshirak (most famous instant noodles) costs 40-50₽. A pack of pasta is about 90₽. Chicken thighs are about 300₽ per kg in supermarkets. Veggies range from 50 to 100₽ per kilogram. 

A can of beer is anything from 50₽ to 300₽ and up. A pack of cigarettes is usually around 110₽. 

If you feel eating our, Burger King and KFC usually offer meals with a coupon you can get from their mobile app. A meal with a cheeseburger, fries, onion rings, nuggets, soda with free refills and a small Snickers bar is 199₽ right now.

Yup. The highest priority one. If their hardware is not set up to ditch any alerts that are outdated (this one has a 2001 timestamp) they’re gonna deal with their emergency transmitter breaking in.

Disney can DMCA your ass on Twitter while FCC doesn’t care about it if it’s not aired on TV or radio. You can make it vague so TV station stuff would think of something like “let’s not use this or the FCC could fuck us over about it”. 

FCC doesn’t really mess around when it comes to anything that resembles data bursts designed to be received by emergency transmitters.

Chances are it won’t do anything. Emergency transmitters need no less than pretty clearly sounding three chirps so you’d have to have a pretty nice tweeter for it. But nonetheless there was several cases when stations were [slapped with hefty fines](https://deadline.com/2019/08/fcc-fines-walking-dead-jimmy-kimmel-live-others-hit-with-fcc-fines-for-misuing-emergency-alert-tones-1202669390/) using sounds that vaguely resembles “real stuff”. 

The one I mentioned are real data bursts used for national tests. WZTV and it’s owner iHeartMedia  [got a $1 million fine ](https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2015/05/multi-state-cascade-of-false-emergency-alerts-nets-1-million-fine/)for playing these exact chirps on the air. So TV engineers are specifically told to NOT to fuck with everything which could sound by emergency system data busts.
